title: Acids, alkalis and pH
keyIdea: pH runs from 0 to 14: below 7 is acidic, 7 is neutral, above 7 is alkaline; indicators show it with colour.

kid: The pH scale runs from 0 to 14. Below 7 is acid, 7 is neutral, and above 7 is alkali.
An indicator changes colour to show pH. Universal indicator is red in strong acid, green when neutral, and purple in strong alkali. Lemon juice is an acid. Soap is an alkali.
adult: Acids release hydrogen ions (H⁺) in water; alkalis release hydroxide ions (OH⁻). The more H⁺, the lower the pH. Each step of 1 on the scale is a tenfold change in H⁺.
Neutralisation: acid + alkali → salt + water, because H⁺ and OH⁻ join to make water. Litmus only says acid or alkali; universal indicator or a pH probe gives a number.

familyTip: Make red-cabbage indicator: boil chopped red cabbage, cool and strain. Test vinegar, soap and baking soda and compare the colours.

practice.explain: pH 2 is well below 7: a strong acid.

pool.explain: Red or blue: acid or alkali, not the number.
